Reusable parameterized models

Source: vignettes/parameterized-models.Rmd
parameterized-models.Rmd
library(optcompR)

optcompR describes an optimization problem once, as variables, expressions, constraints and an objective, and then classifies it, chooses a capable solver Parameters are named constants that stay symbolic in the model. Changing their values does not rebuild expressions: optcompR substitutes the current values when it builds the standard form, and caches that form for each set of values.

Declaring parameters 

m <- opt_model()
x <- opt_variable(m, "x", dim = 2, lower = 0)
d <- opt_parameter(m, "demand", value = 10)
price <- opt_parameter(m, "price", value = c(3, 5))
opt_constraint(m, sum(x) >= d, name = "demand")
opt_constraint(m, x[1] <= 6)
opt_objective(m, sum(price * x))
opt_value(opt_solve(m), x)
#> [1] 6 4

Changing values 

opt_set_parameter(m, price, c(6, 5))
opt_value(opt_solve(m), x)
#> [1]  0 10

Scenario sweeps 

opt_set_parameter(m, price, c(3, 5))
opt_scenarios(m, d, c(4, 8, 12, 16))
#>   scenario value  status objective
#> 1        1     4 optimal        12
#> 2        2     8 optimal        28
#> 3        3    12 optimal        48
#> 4        4    16 optimal        68

The parameter is restored after the sweep. With keep = TRUE the full results are kept in the results attribute.

Parameters in quadratic terms

A product of a parameter and a quadratic term stays quadratic after substitution, so p * x^2 is a QP for every value of p:

m2 <- opt_model()
y <- opt_variable(m2, "y")
p <- opt_parameter(m2, "p", value = 1)
opt_objective(m2, p * y^2 - 4 * y)
opt_classify(m2)$class
#> [1] "QP"
sapply(c(0.5, 1, 2), function(v) {
  opt_set_parameter(m2, p, v)
  opt_value(opt_solve(m2), y)
})
#> [1] 4 2 1

Warm starts

Start values are passed to solvers that accept them (HiGHS for MILP, NLopt for the initial point). Results record whether one was used.

m3 <- opt_model("max")
z <- opt_variable(m3, "z", dim = 3, type = "integer", lower = 0, upper = 5)
opt_constraint(m3, sum(z) <= 7)
opt_objective(m3, sum(c(3, 2, 1) * z))
opt_set_start(m3, z, c(5, 2, 0))
r <- opt_solve(m3)
r$warm_start
#> [1] TRUE

Changing structure

Bounds, types and fixed values can also change between solves:

opt_set_bounds(m3, z[1], upper = 3)
opt_value(opt_solve(m3), z)
#> [1] 3 4 0
opt_fix(m3, z[2], 0)
opt_value(opt_solve(m3), z)
#> [1] 3 0 4
